memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: To Adam he said, "Because you listened to your wife and ate fruit from the tree about which I commanded you, 'You must not eat from it,' cursed is the ground because of you; through painful toil you will eat food from it all the days of your life. It will produce thorns and thistles for you, and you will eat the plants of the field. By the sweat of your brow you will eat your food until you return to the ground, since from it you were taken; for dust you are and to dust you will return." — Gen 3:17–19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God now turns to Adam. Notice the root of the problem: "you listened to your wife" — not because seeking counsel is wrong, but because Adam followed her voice into disobedience over the clear command of God. He let another word overrule God's word, and the whole created order feels the effect.

Work itself was not the curse; Adam had been given good work to do in the garden before any sin (Gen 2:15). But now work becomes toil. The ground that once yielded freely will resist him, bringing thorns and thistles, demanding sweat and struggle. And most sobering of all comes the sentence of death: "dust you are and to dust you will return." The warning God had given (Gen 2:17) now falls.

We feel this every day, don't we? Life is filled with effort that doesn't always yield fruit, with weariness and frustration, and finally with the shadow of death over us all.

Dear friend, but the last Adam entered this cursed ground for us. Jesus knew sweat and toil, wore a crown of the very thorns that marked the curse, and returned to the dust of death — so that He might break its power. Creation still groans, but it groans in hope, waiting for the day it will be set free (Rom 8:20–21). The dust is not our final destiny; resurrection is.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do you feel the "thorns and thistles" of frustrated effort in your own life?
2. How does it help to know that Jesus entered this cursed ground for you?
3. How does the hope of resurrection change the way you face death and toil?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I feel the weariness of living in a world under the curse, where work is hard and death still shadows us. Thank You that Jesus wore the thorns and tasted death to break its power. Fill me with resurrection hope, knowing that You are making all things new. Amen.
